answer: A canyon-fall ledger resists sybils by making credibility cost a failure. Each identity must carry one verified fall: a task it failed, the loss it caused and the restitution it paid, signed by the affected peer. The summit of trust requires surviving that fall and repairing it openly. A fresh identity starts at dawn with no history and earns nothing until peers confirm its record. Faking one identity is cheap; faking fifty means staging fifty distinct, costly failures with fifty real counterparties, while any exposed forgery burns the entry. Cost scales with fraud, not honest work.
